title: Inverted Classroom an der Hochschule Karlsruhe - ein nicht quantisierter Flip
venue: Das Inverted Classroom Model: Begleitband zur ersten deutschen ICM-Konferenz
extended_summary:
This paper discusses the introduction and early evaluation of the Inverted Classroom Model (ICM) at Hochschule Karlsruhe as part of the SKATING project. The central problem is how to improve teaching and reduce student difficulties in engineering-oriented higher education, especially issues related to heterogeneous prior knowledge, limited semester-long studying, and high dropout risk. The authors frame ICM as a potentially useful response because it shifts content delivery outside class and uses class time for guided practice, interaction, and deeper learning.

The approach studied is not a single standardized intervention but a set of pilot implementations of ICM variants, ranging from minimally inverted lecture summaries to partially or fully inverted topics in mathematics. The paper emphasizes careful adaptation to course, instructor, and student needs, and it outlines an evaluation strategy combining student surveys, classroom observation, usage statistics, and course outcomes. In the described pilot, an upper-level engineering mathematics course at Hochschule Karlsruhe was partly inverted using recorded video materials made available through ILIAS and YouTube, with in-class time used for problem solving and discussion.

The authors conclude that ICM can be implemented in a flexible, staged way and may support student engagement, self-paced learning, and richer in-class interaction. However, they stress that success depends on fit with local conditions, student cooperation, and careful evaluation of both intended and unintended effects such as increased workload, technical problems, and differential benefits across learners. The paper is primarily a methodological and reflective report on early implementation rather than a results paper with definitive outcome findings.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative/pilot report with descriptive process evaluation, student feedback, and planned follow-up comparisons, not a controlled experiment. It is peer-reviewed conference/book chapter style academic work, but the evidence base is low on causal credibility.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports promising but unquantified benefits and mainly discusses implementation feasibility and student engagement. Because no effect sizes are reported and the scope is a small pilot, the impact is modest and unclear for broader generalization.

interventions.use_case: inverted classroom implementation using recorded lecture summaries, short instructional videos, forum support, and online materials for K-12/tertiary-style blended learning support

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports a pilot inverted-classroom implementation in higher mathematics (Höhere Mathematik 3) with about 20 students, but provides no numerical effect size. The author describes improved engagement with the topic Differentialgleichungssysteme and plans to compare future exam results against prior years, indicating a positive but still preliminary academic signal rather than a quantified impact.
finding.measure: student understanding/participation in higher mathematics topic sessions; planned comparison of exam results

finding.finding_summary: The article emphasizes increased student motivation, curiosity, and a 'flow' experience as key success criteria, and reports mostly positive student feedback during the pilot. Students noted concerns about missing opportunities to ask questions and possible extra time burden, but the overall reception of the method was favorable.
finding.measure: student feedback, perceived motivation/curiosity, satisfaction surveys, informal responses

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that the inverted classroom supports active problem solving, peer work, and more interaction in class, and observes large in-class phases of guided self-study and partner problem solving. No numerical effect size is reported, but the intended and observed emphasis is on collaboration and self-regulated preparation.
finding.measure: observed collaboration/partner work, self-study behavior, participation in discussion

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports clear implementation and preparation costs: about 1 hour of production time per recording, plus roughly 30 minutes of teacher setup and 30 minutes of organization per session when the professor self-recorded the material. At the same time, it suggests that once materials are created, later semesters may require less effort, so the overall workload effect is mixed and context-dependent.
finding.measure: teacher preparation time, production time, organizational workload

finding.finding_summary: The paper frames the inverted classroom as a potentially scalable reform strategy for improving persistence and making engineering study more feasible, especially at applied universities with heterogeneous entrants. This is a conceptual and pilot-level institutional argument rather than a quantified outcome, but it is clearly positioned as supporting broader teaching reform and study success.
finding.measure: institutional adoption potential, perceived fit for study reform and dropout reduction
